:::{#exr-matmul-product-of-sums-practice}
#### Comparing $(\matr{A} + \matr{B})(\matr{A} + \matr{B})$ with the rule for numbers

For numbers, $(a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2$.
@thm-matmul-product-of-sums expands a [product](#def-matrix-mult) of two [matrix sums](#def-matrix-addition) into four terms instead,
because $\matr{A}\matr{B}$ and $\matr{B}\matr{A}$ can differ.
Let

$$
\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

Is $(\matr{A} + \matr{B})(\matr{A} + \matr{B})$ [equal](#def-matrix-equality) to $\matr{A}\matr{A} + 2\matr{A}\matr{B} + \matr{B}\matr{B}$?

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

Compute $\matr{A} + \matr{B}$ and its [product](#def-matrix-mult) with itself,
then compute $\matr{A}\matr{A}$, $\matr{A}\matr{B}$ and $\matr{B}\matr{B}$ with @def-matrix-mult.

:::
